panels.title: ASR — last 15m
panels.description: Answer-Seizure Ratio = answered_calls / total_calls over the last 15 minutes, on the selected zone. THE headline carrier metric. answered = answer_time IS NOT NULL. Green >= 55%, amber >= 40%, red below.

targets.rawSql: SELECT (count(*) FILTER (WHERE answer_time IS NOT NULL))::float / NULLIF(count(*), 0) AS asr FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND start_time > now() - interval '15 minutes' AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone';

panels.title: Concurrent calls — live
panels.description: Connected (bridged) calls up right now on the selected zone: sum(freeswitch_calls_active{zone=~"$zonere"}) — the live ESL-exporter gauge (:9103, ~10s poll), same source as Traffic Status 'Concurrent calls — live'. Replaces the old CDR-overlap proxy (answer_time <= now() < end_time), which could only see calls whose CDR had already been written — CDRs land at hangup, so it structurally missed in-progress calls. $zonere is derived from the Zone picker (All = every zone). Informational blue; per-zone capacity colouring + the high-water marks are on Traffic Status.

panels.title: CPS — last 1m
panels.description: Calls per second = count of seized calls (by start_time) in the last 60s / 60, on the selected zone. Rated capacity is ~500 CPS per zone; amber/red are set for the all-zones view. See Traffic Status for per-zone / per-node CPS.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*)::float / 60.0 AS cps FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND start_time > now() - interval '1 minute' AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone';

panels.title: Good-or-better calls — last 15m
panels.description: Share of GRADED calls in the last 15 min (selected zone) whose call grade is great or good: 100 × count(call_quality_grade IN great/good) / count(call_quality_grade IS NOT NULL), A rows only. Call-level = the WORSE direction of caller→platform (A row) and the answered carrier callee→platform (B row), stored on the A row by cdr_refresh_call_quality() (migration 50). Only graded calls count: answered, >= 5 s, and either >= 250 inbound packets (rated) or < 10% of the expected inbound packets (no_rtp = one-way audio, graded poor). Grades (plan D, ONE definition, applied to the stored 2-dp E-model MOS): great >= 4.34 (R>=90) · good >= 4.02 (R>=80) · fair >= 3.60 (R>=70) · poor < 3.60 or one-way audio. MOS is our ITU-T G.107 E-model from true RTP sequence loss (G.711 ceiling 4.41), not FreeSWITCH's estimator. Red < 90% · amber < 97% · green >= 97% (the SLI 1 target, infra/monitoring/SLOS.md). '—' = no graded call in the window.

targets.rawSql: SELECT 100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE call_quality_grade IN ('great','good')) / NULLIF(count(*) FILTER (WHERE call_quality_grade IS NOT NULL), 0) AS good_or_better_pct FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND call_quality_grade IS NOT NULL AND start_time > now() - interval '15 minutes' AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone';

panels.title: On-net % — last 15m
panels.description: Share of calls short-circuited internally (carrier hairpin avoided): count(*) FILTER (WHERE on_net) / count(*). New internal-routing metric. on_net is a boolean set by FreeSWITCH; NULL/false = off-net.

targets.rawSql: SELECT (count(*) FILTER (WHERE on_net))::float / NULLIF(count(*), 0) AS on_net_pct FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND start_time > now() - interval '15 minutes' AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone';

panels.title: Call MOS — p50 / p10 (10m)
panels.description: Median and 10th-percentile (worst decile) CALL MOS per 10m, selected zone: percentile_cont over call_mos of A rows with call_quality_status='rated' (one-way-audio calls have no MOS and are on the one-way panel instead). Call-level = the WORSE direction of caller→platform (A row) and the answered carrier callee→platform (B row), stored on the A row by cdr_refresh_call_quality() (migration 50). Only graded calls count: answered, >= 5 s, and either >= 250 inbound packets (rated) or < 10% of the expected inbound packets (no_rtp = one-way audio, graded poor). Dashed lines = the grade cut points 3.60 (fair) / 4.02 (good) / 4.34 (great). No averages — percentiles only. A clean G.711 call is 4.41.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '10m') AS time, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY call_mos) AS "p50 call MOS", percentile_cont(0.1) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY call_mos) AS "p10 call MOS" FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND call_quality_status = 'rated' AND call_mos IS NOT NULL AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: True packet loss — p95 by direction (10m)
panels.description: p95 of packet_loss_pct per 10m, selected zone, split by direction. packet_loss_pct is TRUE RTP sequence loss (RFC 3550 expected − received, patched FS) or FS's lossrate (legacy images / history), no longer flaws÷packets. Leg-level panel: rows with quality_status='rated' (answered >= 5 s, >= 250 inbound packets, loss input present). caller→platform = the A row (leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B', what the callee hears); callee→platform = the carrier B rows (leg='B', what the caller hears). Deliberately leg-aware — B rows are directions here, never counted as calls. Loss colours (plan D): <= 4% green · <= 8% amber · > 8% red; ~1% random loss already costs 0.08 MOS on G.711.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '10m') AS time, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY packet_loss_pct) FILTER (WHERE caller_side) AS "caller→platform p95", percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY packet_loss_pct) FILTER (WHERE NOT caller_side) AS "callee→platform p95" FROM (SELECT start_time, packet_loss_pct, (leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B') AS caller_side FROM cdrs WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND quality_status = 'rated' AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' AND packet_loss_pct IS NOT NULL) s GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Per-zone call volume — hourly
panels.description: Seized calls per hour per zone as one line per zone (zone from freeswitch_node). Watch load balance across East / West / Central. All zones shown regardless of the Zone filter.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '1h') AS time, CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END AS zone, count(*) AS calls FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Total call volume — hourly
panels.description: Whole-platform offered volume: seized calls per hour from raw cdrs over the range (all zones). The headline traffic curve.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '1h') AS time, count(*) AS calls FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: SIP response classes — over time
panels.description: sip_code bucketed into response classes, 10-minutely, selected zone. NULL sip_code (never got a final response) shown as 'none'. A growing 4xx/5xx band is the earliest sign of a carrier/routing fault.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '10m') AS time, CASE WHEN sip_code IS NULL THEN 'none' WHEN sip_code BETWEEN 200 AND 299 THEN '2xx' WHEN sip_code BETWEEN 300 AND 399 THEN '3xx' WHEN sip_code BETWEEN 400 AND 499 THEN '4xx' WHEN sip_code BETWEEN 500 AND 599 THEN '5xx' WHEN sip_code BETWEEN 600 AND 699 THEN '6xx' ELSE 'other' END AS class, count(*) AS calls FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Carrier split — inbound by carrier / PoP (10m)
panels.description: Inbound (direction='inbound') seized calls per 10m, one series per ingress carrier-PoP from cdrs.inbound_carrier + inbound_carrier_pop (stamped spoof-proof by Kamailio from the verified source IP; FS records them as channel vars). Series values are bounded: bandwidth-dallas / bandwidth-la / bandwidth-ny / bandwidth-atlanta, sinch-denver / sinch-chicago, bare 'bandwidth' = trusted-but-unmapped Bandwidth IP or pre-attribution rows (NULL folded to bandwidth — it was the only orig carrier then). A Sinch orig test call (test TNs 5305480845 Denver / 5305480846 Chicago) appears here as a sinch-denver / sinch-chicago bump once the call hangs up and its CDR lands. Honours the Zone filter.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '10m') AS time, COALESCE(inbound_carrier, 'bandwidth') || COALESCE('-' || NULLIF(inbound_carrier_pop, ''), '') AS carrier_pop, count(*) AS calls FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND direction = 'inbound' AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Quality detail — grades / loss / jitter / one-way audio (graded legs only)
Jitter (RFC 3550) — p50 / p95 by direction (10m)
panels.description: p50 and p95 of the per-call MEAN RFC 3550 interarrival jitter (jitter_avg_ms, kernel receive timestamps) per 10m, selected zone, split by direction. Leg-level panel: rows with quality_status='rated' (answered >= 5 s, >= 250 inbound packets, loss input present). caller→platform = the A row (leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B', what the callee hears); callee→platform = the carrier B rows (leg='B', what the caller hears). Deliberately leg-aware — B rows are directions here, never counted as calls. EMPTY until the FreeSWITCH images carry quality patch v1 — legacy images and history store jitter NULL (the old value was fabricated from FS's running variance and is kept only as fs_jitter_max_std_ms). Diagnostic only: jitter does not enter the MOS. <= 20 ms green · <= 50 amber · > 50 red.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '10m') AS time, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY jitter_avg_ms) FILTER (WHERE caller_side) AS "caller→platform p50", percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY jitter_avg_ms) FILTER (WHERE caller_side) AS "caller→platform p95", percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY jitter_avg_ms) FILTER (WHERE NOT caller_side) AS "callee→platform p50", percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY jitter_avg_ms) FILTER (WHERE NOT caller_side) AS "callee→platform p95" FROM (SELECT start_time, jitter_avg_ms, (leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B') AS caller_side FROM cdrs WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND quality_status = 'rated' AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' AND jitter_avg_ms IS NOT NULL) s GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Call grade distribution
panels.description: Graded calls in the dashboard range (selected zone, A rows) by CALL grade — the worse direction. Great >= 4.34 · Good >= 4.02 · Fair >= 3.60 · Poor (audio) = graded poor with media both ways (MOS < 3.60) · One-way / no audio = call_quality_status='no_rtp' (one side sent < 10% of the expected packets; also graded poor). Call-level = the WORSE direction of caller→platform (A row) and the answered carrier callee→platform (B row), stored on the A row by cdr_refresh_call_quality() (migration 50). Only graded calls count: answered, >= 5 s, and either >= 250 inbound packets (rated) or < 10% of the expected inbound packets (no_rtp = one-way audio, graded poor). All five bands always render (fixed VALUES list LEFT JOIN) so the axis never collapses. Ungraded calls (unanswered, < 5 s, too few packets, no media data) are excluded — see the snapshot's 'Not graded'.

targets.rawSql: SELECT b.band AS band, COALESCE(a.calls, 0) AS calls FROM (VALUES (1, 'Great'), (2, 'Good'), (3, 'Fair'), (4, 'Poor (audio)'), (5, 'One-way / no audio')) AS b(ord, band) LEFT JOIN (SELECT CASE WHEN call_quality_status = 'no_rtp' THEN 'One-way / no audio' WHEN call_quality_grade = 'great' THEN 'Great' WHEN call_quality_grade = 'good' THEN 'Good' WHEN call_quality_grade = 'fair' THEN 'Fair' WHEN call_quality_grade = 'poor' THEN 'Poor (audio)' END AS band, count(*) AS calls FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND call_quality_grade IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1) a ON a.band = b.band ORDER BY b.ord;

panels.title: Loss distribution — graded legs
panels.description: Rated legs in the dashboard range (selected zone) bucketed by true packet_loss_pct, one bar per direction per band: 0 · (0, 0.5) · [0.5, 1) · [1, 2) · [2, 4) · [4, 8) · >= 8 %. At random loss (G.711 + PLC) the grade boundaries fall at ~0.87% (great), ~4.05% (good) and ~8.11% (fair). Leg-level panel: rows with quality_status='rated' (answered >= 5 s, >= 250 inbound packets, loss input present). caller→platform = the A row (leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B', what the callee hears); callee→platform = the carrier B rows (leg='B', what the caller hears). Deliberately leg-aware — B rows are directions here, never counted as calls. All seven bands always render. Replaces the old R-factor trend (an average of a relabelled MOS).

targets.rawSql: SELECT b.band AS band, COALESCE(a.caller, 0) AS "caller→platform", COALESCE(a.callee, 0) AS "callee→platform" FROM (VALUES (1, '0%'), (2, '0–0.5%'), (3, '0.5–1%'), (4, '1–2%'), (5, '2–4%'), (6, '4–8%'), (7, '≥8%')) AS b(ord, band) LEFT JOIN (SELECT CASE WHEN packet_loss_pct = 0 THEN '0%' WHEN packet_loss_pct < 0.5 THEN '0–0.5%' WHEN packet_loss_pct < 1 THEN '0.5–1%' WHEN packet_loss_pct < 2 THEN '1–2%' WHEN packet_loss_pct < 4 THEN '2–4%' WHEN packet_loss_pct < 8 THEN '4–8%' ELSE '≥8%' END AS band, count(*) FILTER (WHERE caller_side) AS caller, count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT caller_side) AS callee FROM (SELECT start_time, packet_loss_pct, (leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B') AS caller_side FROM cdrs WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND quality_status = 'rated' AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' AND packet_loss_pct IS NOT NULL) s GROUP BY 1) a ON a.band = b.band ORDER BY b.ord;

panels.title: One-way / no inbound audio — per hour
panels.description: Per hour, selected zone. Silent = legs with quality_status='no_rtp': answered >= 5 s but < 10% of the expected inbound RTP packets (one-way audio — typically a media-path fault: Cloud NAT / bypass-vpn, SDP c=, RTP source IP). caller→platform silent = the A row (the callee heard nothing); callee→platform silent = a carrier B row (the caller heard nothing). Partial inbound media = rated or low_sample legs, either direction, that received < 50% of the packets their talk time implies (inbound_media_ratio < 0.5) — audio that died mid-call, which early media can hide from no_rtp. Leg-level and deliberately leg-aware. The paging half is scripts/backup/media_guard.sh (revup-alert). Replaces the old FS 'Quality %' trend.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '1h') AS time, count(*) FILTER (WHERE caller_side) AS "caller→platform silent", count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT caller_side) AS "callee→platform silent" FROM (SELECT start_time, (leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B') AS caller_side FROM cdrs WHERE $__timeFilter(start_time) AND quality_status = 'no_rtp' AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone') s GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '1h') AS time, count(*) FILTER (WHERE quality_status IN ('rated','low_sample') AND inbound_media_ratio < 0.5) AS "partial inbound media" FROM cdrs WHERE (leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' OR leg = 'B') AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND quality_status IN ('rated','low_sample') AND inbound_media_ratio < 0.5 AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Delivery — answered vs failed / ASR trends / ACD / PDD
Answered vs failed — per 5m
panels.description: Seized calls bucketed 5-minutely into answered (answer_time present) vs failed (never answered). Stacked. A rising failed band with flat answered = a routing/carrier problem.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '5m') AS time, count(*) FILTER (WHERE answer_time IS NOT NULL) AS answered, count(*) FILTER (WHERE answer_time IS NULL) AS failed FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: ASR trend per zone — hourly
panels.description: Answer-Seizure Ratio per zone per hour from raw cdrs (cdr_hourly_stats has no sbc_id, so zone attribution needs raw rows). answered / seized. Spans all zones side by side; NOT filtered by the Zone variable so zones can be compared.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '1h') AS time, CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END AS zone, (count(*) FILTER (WHERE answer_time IS NOT NULL))::float / NULLIF(count(*), 0) AS asr FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: ASR trend per carrier — hourly
panels.description: ASR per carrier_used per hour on the selected zone — one series per carrier value, so table-driven trunks (bandwidth-dallas, bandwidth-la, sinch-atlanta-ld, sinch-denver-tf, future carriers) appear automatically. Legacy enum rows are folded to readable labels: carrier_primary -> bandwidth-dallas, carrier_secondary -> bandwidth-la (the East/Central mapping; pre-fold West rows labeled these enums the same way even though West's primary PoP was LA). 'local'/'default'/NULL excluded. Divergence between lines pinpoints a carrier/PoP-side answer problem.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '1h') AS time, CASE carrier_used WHEN 'carrier_primary' THEN 'bandwidth-dallas' WHEN 'carrier_secondary' THEN 'bandwidth-la' ELSE carrier_used END AS carrier, (count(*) FILTER (WHERE answer_time IS NOT NULL))::float / NULLIF(count(*), 0) AS asr FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND carrier_used IS NOT NULL AND carrier_used NOT IN ('local','default','') AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: ACD — avg call duration (hourly)
panels.description: Average answered-call duration in seconds, from cdr_hourly_stats.avg_duration_sec (already answered-only, cheap continuous aggregate). Customer-scoped aggregate has no zone dimension, so this is all-zones. Restricted to direction='inbound' (2026-09-23 A/B leg split): carrier B-leg rows (leg='B', direction='outbound') land in this aggregate too, and the CAGG has no leg dimension, so the direction key is what keeps this one-row-per-call; outbound-originated calls (API/trunk outbound A-legs) are excluded as a side effect. A sudden ACD collapse often means calls answering then failing fast (dead air / media).

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(hour, '1h') AS time, sum(total_duration_sec)::float / NULLIF(sum(answered_calls), 0) AS acd_sec FROM cdr_hourly_stats WHERE $__timeFilter(hour) AND direction = 'inbound' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: PDD proxy — p50 / p95 time-to-answer (10m)
panels.description: APPROXIMATION of Post-Dial Delay: percentiles of (answer_time - start_time) over answered calls, 10-minute buckets, selected zone. This is CDR time-to-ANSWER, not true PDD to the first 18x provisional — true PDD needs Homer/SIP timing. Watch p95 for carrier slowness.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '10m') AS time, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (answer_time - start_time))) AS p50_s, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (answer_time - start_time))) AS p95_s FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND answer_time IS NOT NULL AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Carrier detail — share / per-carrier ASR / egress / live ingress
Carrier share — range total
panels.description: Share of calls by carrier_used over the range + zone. carrier_primary=Dallas, carrier_secondary=LA, local=on-net, default=unset. Heavy 'secondary' means primary is failing over. Range-aggregate pie over the selected range + zone (the time-based split lives in the priority band).

targets.rawSql: SELECT CASE carrier_used WHEN 'carrier_primary' THEN 'Dallas (primary)' WHEN 'carrier_secondary' THEN 'LA (secondary)' WHEN 'local' THEN 'On-net (local)' WHEN 'default' THEN 'Unset (default)' ELSE COALESCE(carrier_used, 'null') END AS carrier, count(*) AS calls FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

panels.title: ASR by inbound carrier — hourly
panels.description: Answer-Seizure Ratio per INGRESS carrier per hour (inbound legs only) — the origination-side counterpart of the egress 'ASR trend per carrier' panel above (same value-agnostic pattern: one series per cdrs.inbound_carrier value, so any carrier admitted via carrier_trunks appears automatically). Today that is 'bandwidth' vs 'sinch' (NULL pre-attribution rows folded to bandwidth). A sinch line diverging below the bandwidth line = calls arriving via Sinch are failing to answer — an origination-path problem, not a destination problem. Honours the Zone filter.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '1h') AS time, COALESCE(inbound_carrier, 'bandwidth') AS inbound_carrier, (count(*) FILTER (WHERE answer_time IS NOT NULL))::float / NULLIF(count(*), 0) AS asr FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND direction = 'inbound' AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Egress volume by carrier trunk — hourly
panels.description: Outbound B-leg volume per egress trunk per hour from carrier_used — the volume companion of the 'ASR trend per carrier' panel (same value-agnostic fold: carrier_primary -> bandwidth-dallas, carrier_secondary -> bandwidth-la; table-driven values like sinch-atlanta-ld / sinch-denver-tf pass through untouched, so a Sinch TERMINATION sign-off attempt shows here as its own series the hour it happens — carrier_used records the winning/last bridge attempt). 'local' (on-net) / 'default' / NULL excluded. Honours the Zone filter.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '1h') AS time, CASE carrier_used WHEN 'carrier_primary' THEN 'bandwidth-dallas' WHEN 'carrier_secondary' THEN 'bandwidth-la' ELSE carrier_used END AS carrier, count(*) AS calls FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND carrier_used IS NOT NULL AND carrier_used NOT IN ('local','default','') AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Live carrier ingress — SBC admits per 5m
panels.description:
LIVE ingress from the SBCs, not the CDR: sum by trunk of increase(kamailio_trunk_cps{direction='inbound'}[5m]) — Kamailio increments this xhttp_prom counter (NO _total suffix) once per admitted inbound INVITE, so a Sinch orig test call shows a ~1-call bump on the 'sinch' series within a scrape interval, while the call is still up and before its CDR exists. Trunk label is a closed enum: tc1 / tc2 / tc4 = Bandwidth trunk configs (tc4 = default PoPs), 'sinch' = Sinch origination (both PoPs — the label reports INGRESS carrier even though Sinch-originated calls egress via the tc4 Bandwidth config). All zones summed — the Zone variable is SQL-LIKE shaped and does not apply to PromQL panels; per-zone CPS lives on Traffic Status.

Served by vmalert recording rule `trunk:kamailio_trunk_cps:increase5m` (30s eval). Raw fallback query: `sum by (trunk) (increase(kamailio_trunk_cps{direction="inbound"}[5m]))`. Recorded series only exist from the recording-rule deploy timestamp onward - on a now-6h wall any pre-deploy gap ages out within 6h. All zones (Kamailio metric, not zone-filtered).

panels.title: Answered vs failed by inbound carrier / PoP
panels.description: Answer/failure distribution per ingress carrier-PoP over the range + zone (inbound legs only): calls, answered (answer_time present), failed (never answered), ASR%. One row per (inbound_carrier, inbound_carrier_pop); '—' = no PoP attribution (trusted-but-unmapped Bandwidth IP or pre-attribution rows). This is the sign-off table for Sinch origination validation: a test call to 5305480845/46 must produce a sinch/denver or sinch/chicago row with calls>=1. Scoped to the selected range + zone.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(inbound_carrier, 'bandwidth') AS carrier, COALESCE(NULLIF(inbound_carrier_pop, ''), '—') AS pop, count(*) AS calls, count(*) FILTER (WHERE answer_time IS NOT NULL) AS answered, count(*) FILTER (WHERE answer_time IS NULL) AS failed, round(100.0 * (count(*) FILTER (WHERE answer_time IS NOT NULL)) / NULLIF(count(*), 0), 1) AS asr_pct FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND direction = 'inbound' AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY calls DESC;

panels.title: Top hangup causes
panels.description: FreeSWITCH hangup_cause counts + share over the range + zone. NORMAL_CLEARING dominates healthy traffic; spikes in NO_ANSWER / USER_BUSY / CALL_REJECTED / NORMAL_TEMPORARY_FAILURE point at destination or carrier problems. Top 15. Scoped to the selected range + zone.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(hangup_cause, 'UNKNOWN') AS hangup_cause, count(*) AS calls, round(100.0 * count(*) / NULLIF(sum(count(*)) OVER (), 0), 2) AS pct FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY calls DESC LIMIT 15;

panels.title: Abnormal teardown per hour
panels.description: Calls per hour whose hangup_cause says the leg was NOT torn down by a BYE but by a timer: MEDIA_TIMEOUT (RTP silence, 60s), RECOVERY_ON_TIMER_EXPIRE (session timer, <=30m), ALLOTTED_TIMEOUT (bridge/originate timeout). A cluster of these right after an SBC failover = BYEs that got 481/408 (see vmalert SipByeFailureShare / FsStaleChannels in docker/vmalert/rules/teardown.yml). One line per cause. Scoped to the selected range + zone, same SQL shape as Top hangup causes.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(start_time, '1h') AS time, hangup_cause AS metric, count(*) AS calls FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND hangup_cause IN ('MEDIA_TIMEOUT','RECOVERY_ON_TIMER_EXPIRE','ALLOTTED_TIMEOUT') AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Graded-call quality snapshot
panels.description: Call-level quality over the current range + zone, A rows (one per call). Graded calls = count(call_quality_grade). Good+ % = great/good share of graded. Poor % includes one-way audio. p10 call MOS = worst-decile MOS of rated calls. One-way audio calls = call_quality_status='no_rtp'. Not graded = every other A row in range (unanswered, < 5 s, too few packets, no media data) — if it dwarfs Graded calls the quality panels are a small sample. Grades (plan D, ONE definition, applied to the stored 2-dp E-model MOS): great >= 4.34 (R>=90) · good >= 4.02 (R>=80) · fair >= 3.60 (R>=70) · poor < 3.60 or one-way audio. MOS is our ITU-T G.107 E-model from true RTP sequence loss (G.711 ceiling 4.41), not FreeSWITCH's estimator. No averages.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(call_quality_grade) AS "Graded calls", 100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE call_quality_grade IN ('great','good')) / NULLIF(count(call_quality_grade), 0) AS "Good+ %", 100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE call_quality_grade = 'poor') / NULLIF(count(call_quality_grade), 0) AS "Poor % (incl. one-way)", percentile_cont(0.1) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY call_mos) FILTER (WHERE call_quality_status = 'rated' AND call_mos IS NOT NULL) AS "p10 call MOS", count(*) FILTER (WHERE call_quality_status = 'no_rtp') AS "One-way audio calls", count(*) FILTER (WHERE call_quality_grade IS NULL) AS "Not graded" FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND $__timeFilter(start_time) AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone';

panels.title: Carrier legs per call — last 24h (orphan-leg check)
panels.description: STAFF / cutover check for the CDR A/B leg split (docs/CDR_LEG_SPLIT_CONTRACT.md). Fixed 24h window (ignores the time picker), follows the Zone filter. Every other cdrs panel on this board counts ONE row per call (leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B'); this panel is the only one that reads B rows (leg='B', one per carrier bridge attempt, direction='outbound'). B rows = carrier-attempt rows; Calls (A) with >=1 B = distinct calls whose A row exists and has at least one B row; Max / Avg leg_attempt = highest attempt number per call (failover depth; 1 = first attempt answered or failed with no retry, up to 4 = 2 SBC x 2 carrier loop). Orphan B rows = B rows whose call_id has NO A row (a.uuid = b.call_id) and whose call's first attempt started >3h ago — MUST be 0; >0 means the ingest dropped/misattributed an A-leg or wrote a B row with a bad cdr_call_id (red). B awaiting A (<3h) = same test for younger calls: an A-leg CDR is only posted at call hangup, so a call still in progress legitimately has B rows (failed attempts) and no A row yet — informational only. All zero before log-b-leg is enabled on a zone's FreeSWITCH.

targets.rawSql: WITH b AS (SELECT call_id, leg_attempt, start_time FROM cdrs WHERE leg = 'B' AND start_time > now() - interval '24 hours' AND CASE WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'west%' THEN 'west' WHEN freeswitch_node LIKE 'central%' THEN 'central' WHEN COALESCE(freeswitch_node,'') = '' THEN 'unknown' ELSE 'east' END LIKE '$zone'), per_call AS (SELECT call_id, count(*) AS b_rows, max(leg_attempt) AS max_attempt, min(start_time) AS first_b, EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cdrs a WHERE a.uuid = b.call_id AND a.leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND a.start_time > now() - interval '25 hours') AS has_a FROM b GROUP BY call_id) SELECT COALESCE(sum(b_rows), 0) AS "B rows", count(*) FILTER (WHERE has_a) AS "Calls (A) with >=1 B", max(max_attempt) AS "Max leg_attempt", avg(max_attempt) AS "Avg leg_attempt / call", COALESCE(sum(b_rows) FILTER (WHERE NOT has_a AND first_b < now() - interval '3 hours'), 0) AS "Orphan B rows", COALESCE(sum(b_rows) FILTER (WHERE NOT has_a AND first_b >= now() - interval '3 hours'), 0) AS "B awaiting A (<3h)" FROM per_call;

list.name: zone
list.label: Zone
list.description: Filter raw-cdrs panels by zone, derived from freeswitch_node (one FS per zone). 'All' = SQL LIKE '%'. Note: the hourly-aggregate panels (ACD, and the per-zone ASR panel) and the live Kamailio ingress panel (PromQL) span all zones regardless of this filter. The live 'Concurrent calls' stat (PromQL) DOES follow it, via the derived hidden $zonere.
list.query: All : %, East : east, West : west, Central : central

list.name: zonere
list.label: Zone (regex)
list.description: Hidden regex twin of $zone for the PromQL (VictoriaMetrics) panels (used as zone=~"$zonere"). DERIVED from $zone by a trivial Postgres query (All '%' -> '.*', else the zone name), so it follows the Zone picker automatically — unlike a static custom twin, which a hidden variable cannot be switched by hand. This board is CDR/Postgres-driven already, so the query adds no new dependency.
list.definition: SELECT CASE WHEN '$zone' = '%' THEN '.*' ELSE '$zone' END AS zonere
list.query: SELECT CASE WHEN '$zone' = '%' THEN '.*' ELSE '$zone' END AS zonere

title: Call Quality
description: Call Quality wall board — the full voice picture from the CDR hypertable (voip-cdr-pg). Top strip: last-15m live snapshot (ASR / Concurrent / CPS / Good-or-better calls / On-net %) on the selected zone. Priority band (two rows of three): call MOS p50/p10, true packet loss p95 by direction, per-zone volume, total volume, SIP response classes, and THE carrier split — inbound by carrier / PoP (Bandwidth vs Sinch), attribution from cdrs.inbound_carrier / inbound_carrier_pop stamped spoof-proof by Kamailio at carrier ingress. Below, themed rows: quality detail (RFC 3550 jitter by direction / call grade distribution / loss distribution / one-way audio per hour), delivery (answered-vs-failed, ASR trends, ACD, PDD), carrier detail (egress share from carrier_used, per-carrier ASR, plus a live Kamailio ingress counter that shows a call at INVITE time — before its CDR exists), and diagnostics (hangup causes, graded-call snapshot). Long trends use the cheap continuous aggregate cdr_hourly_stats (customer-scoped, no zone/carrier dimension — those trends span all zones); recent/quality panels read raw cdrs and honour the Zone filter. PDD is approximated as answer_time - start_time (time-to-answer) — true PDD to the first 18x needs Homer/SIP timing, not the CDR. Infrastructure health (VMs / VIPs / media nodes) lives on the Infrastructure / Home / Fleet dashboards. QUALITY (2026-09, docs/CALL_QUALITY_ACCURACY_PLAN.md): MOS is our ITU-T G.107 E-model from true RTP sequence loss (G.711 ceiling 4.41), graded ONCE — great >= 4.34 · good >= 4.02 · fair >= 3.60 · poor < 3.60 or one-way audio; only evidence-backed calls are graded (answered >= 5 s with >= 250 inbound packets, or one-way audio). Quality panels show shares and percentiles, never MOS averages. CDR A/B leg split (2026-09-23): cdrs holds one A row per call plus one B row per carrier bridge attempt (leg='B'); every call-counting raw-cdrs panel filters leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' (one row per call; call-level grade = the worse direction, stored on the A row). Leg-aware panels: the per-direction quality panels (loss p95, jitter, loss distribution, one-way audio — caller→platform = A row, callee→platform = B row) and 'Carrier legs per call' in Diagnostics. ACD (cdr_hourly_stats) is restricted to direction='inbound' so outbound B rows in the aggregate are excluded.
